Anyone considering going there should think carefully. My girlfriend had one or two fillings done, I'm not sure which, and it cost 2700 baht, including everything and anesthetic. It was the most expensive filling I've ever seen. A week later, she experienced severe tooth pain and sensitivity. She wanted to see the doctor who performed the filling, so she went back to the clinic. However, the doctor only comes to the clinic twice a month, and appointments often didn't match. In the end, she had an appointment a month after the filling. During that time, she continued to experience pain. After work, she went to see another doctor who was excellent. This doctor said she could have the tooth extracted if she wanted, free of charge. But because she was experiencing severe sensitivity, she didn't opt ​​for extraction. She waited until her appointment with the original doctor, who said everything was normal, the filling equipment was fine, and that the problem might be with the root. He said there would be a charge for extraction. She was very disappointed and decided to go elsewhere.
In summary:
As a doctor, you should see the patient's tooth during the examination. You can't just fill a tooth without proper examination, especially if it's not possible to have a filling done, requiring root canal treatment or other procedures. Think carefully before considering going there. The doctor is in here infrequently; you're lucky, but if you're unlucky, you'll have the same experience as my girlfriend. It was so disappointing, waiting for the doctor in charge of her case.
